claims.statement: The deepagents.middleware package re-exports its public middleware classes and supporting types for filesystem, summarization, skills (including SkillToolResolver), subagents, async subagents, memory, rubric, and unsupported content from its __init__.py, defining the surface consumers import from deepagents.middleware.

Graph construction builds a core stack of filesystem, optional synchronous subagents, parent notification, summarization, tool-call repair, and optional asynchronous subagents; profile middleware, optional skills, provider caching, optional memory, HITL, and unsupported-content filtering form the tail. Caller middleware replaces a same-named entry in place or otherwise lands after the core, and profile-controlled tool exclusion is appended last.

The final _ToolExclusionMiddleware removes profile-excluded tools from model requests and returns an error for matching calls at the tool boundary, but its implementation documents this as advertised-tool consistency rather than a security surface.

The synchronous task tool runs a selected declarative or compiled subagent and returns one parent ToolMessage, serializing structured_response when present or otherwise selecting the last non-empty AIMessage text; forked declarative subagents receive effective compacted history and refuse recursive task delegation.

An isolated AsyncSubAgent launch sends only its description, while experimental fork mode serializes the parent’s effective summarized conversation and task after removing artifacts and rehydrating offloaded media; the remote agent owns its own prompt and tools, and a url-less local ASGI transport requires asynchronous parent invocation.

The summarization factory chooses fraction-based trigger, retention, and argument-truncation defaults when the resolved model profile supplies max_input_tokens, and falls back to fixed token and message thresholds otherwise; it rejects a string rather than a resolved BaseChatModel.

Summarization retains raw message state and records private event and session state; a later request reconstructs its effective history from the summary message and cutoff, while evicted messages are appended to a session-specific backend history file.

The default Deep Agents summary prompt explains that offloaded media references must be preserved and may be read later, while automatic summarization converts inline media to backend references before archive and summary generation.

SummarizationToolMiddleware registers the explicit compact_conversation tool but never compacts automatically; it shares summarization event state with the automatic engine, gates execution until roughly half the automatic trigger, and reports no-op or compaction failure through ToolMessages without updating the event.

The public catalog exposes filesystem permissions, memory, skills and skill-tool resolution as middleware extension points; graph assembly supplies filesystem automatically and conditionally installs skills and memory from create_deep_agent configuration.

The internal message-eviction helper is shared by filesystem middleware and summarization overflow recovery: it offloads a large tool result only when the backend write succeeds, replaces text with a line-numbered head-and-tail preview and preserves non-text blocks, and otherwise leaves the original message intact.

AsyncSubAgentMiddleware provides launch, check, update, cancel, and list tools for remote Agent Protocol work; it persists merge-reduced async_tasks records containing remote identifiers, status, timestamps, and queued-run lineage, validates nonempty unique specifications plus supported modes and update strategies, and uses asynchronous lifecycle hooks to poll unfinished work and give the model another turn after a newly observed outcome.

RubricMiddleware is inactive without a rubric in invocation state; otherwise it initializes private iteration state, grades at natural agent completion, can jump back to the model for revision, and leaves the last model response unchanged for failed, grader-error, or max-iteration outcomes.

UnsupportedContentMiddleware evaluates the resolved request model late in the stack and copies only human and tool messages whose blocks need replacement, preserving the original thread so a later capable model can receive the original multimodal content.

FilesystemMiddleware provides filesystem tools through BackendProtocol, conditionally adds execution for SandboxBackendProtocol, and can evict oversized tool results to backend storage so model context is not saturated.

FilesystemPermission supports allow, deny, and interrupt effects for read/write path rules; permission paths must be absolute without '..' or '~', and real filesystem backends check both the requested and symlink-resolved target paths.

MemoryMiddleware loads configured sources only when private memory_contents is absent, skips missing files but raises on other download errors, and injects formatted memory into each model request unless its system prompt is disabled.

SkillsMiddleware caches source metadata in state per thread with later duplicate names overriding earlier sources; setting skills_metadata to None requests a reload, while pinned skills append their readable instructions before the next model call.

Skill-declared tools are disclosed only after the relevant skill is read or pinned, with the disclosure recorded in state; the middleware resolves eligible tools again at the tool boundary and leaves undisclosed calls invalid.

Prompt-caching assembly always appends Anthropic caching with unsupported-model behavior ignored and conditionally appends Bedrock and Fireworks caching when their optional middleware imports are available.
PatchToolCallsMiddleware runs before an agent to add error ToolMessages for AI-message tool calls lacking recorded results, including malformed or interrupted calls.
TodoListMiddleware is not part of the default main or general-purpose subagent stacks; it can be enabled explicitly or injected through a harness profile's extra_middleware for both stacks.

The manual-compaction factory resolves a model string, constructs a model-aware summarization engine, and registers only SummarizationToolMiddleware; automatic compaction requires separately registering SummarizationMiddleware, which create_deep_agent already adds by default.

Automatic summarization first projects raw messages through any prior event, can truncate older large tool-call arguments, and on compaction persists the new event and session ID while leaving raw messages intact; archive failure produces an event with no recovery path rather than blocking compaction.
